subject: informative gamma priors for the precisions in the hierarchical rw1 model

messages.author: 3ab4461ff960be07
messages.subject: informative gamma priors for the precisions in the hierarchical rw1 model
parts:
Dear INLA-experts,

  

Could you please suggest how to introduce informative gamma priors for the precisions in the hierarchical random walk plus noise model?

For example, the attached picture ("1101-1") shows the fitted values from such a model. I want to decrease overfitting and make “fit.0.025quant” and “fit.0.975quant” (somewhat) wider.

Could you guys please suggest how I should change the code below so as to alter a Gamma prior on the precision of a rw1 model and decrease precision for the id.b0 effect?

I have attached the code, data and the initial results.    

 

Julian Faraway on his website https://julianfaraway.github.io/brinla/examples/rbd.html  lists one possible suggestion for that. I have tried to implement it in this example, but it didn’t help


Code:

g <- n_distinct(data$group)
n <- n_distinct(data$id.b0)

re.b0 <- rep(1:g, each = n)

data <-
  cbind.data.frame(
    data,
    re.b0
  )


formula <- response ~ -1 +
  f(id.b0,
    model = "rw1",
    constr = FALSE,
    replicate = re.b0)

model <- inla(
  formula,
  data = data,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(
    dic = TRUE,
    waic = TRUE,
    cpo = TRUE,
    config = TRUE
  )
)

 
fit.model.H1 <- model$summary.fitted.values
fit.model.H1$group <- data$group


obs.fit.model.H1 <-
  cbind.data.frame(data[, c(1, 3, 2)], fit.0.025quant = fit.model.H1[, c(3)],
                   fit.0.975quant = fit.model.H1[, c(5)], fit.mean = fit.model.H1[, c(1)])

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] informative gamma priors for the precisions in the hierarchical rw1 model
parts:
use f(..., model="rw2", scale.model=TRUE,
hyper=list(prec=list(prior="pc.prec",
param=c(A,0.1)))

which will give marginal stdev, after integration out the precision, of
0.31*A,

for poisson counts and log-link, I would use A=1 or A=0.5, similar for
binomial


for resons discussed in the pc-prior paper (Stat sci'17), I do not
longer use gamma-priors for precions in applications

Best
Havard
